Design shipped the styles: the column under the pointer lights up and the dragged card dims (drag_and_drop.css).

{ "returncode": 0, "output": "# Fizzy Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository. Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments. ## Deploy Default branch: `main` Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`. ## SaaS mode For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions. ## Architecture Overview ### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based) Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**: - Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes - URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...` - Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account` - The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path - Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions - Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context **Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler. ### Authentication & Authorization Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records. ### Entropy System Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity: - Account-level default entropy period - Board-level entropy override - Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating - Configurable via Account/Board settings ### UUID Primary Keys All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings): - Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests - Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records - `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests ### Background Jobs (Solid Queue) Database-backed job queue (no Redis): - Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob - Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account` - Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`. ### Sharded Full-Text Search Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`. ### Imports and exports Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances: - Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported) - Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB) - Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file` ## Coding style Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md. ---- <% card_data = { navigable_list_target: "item", css_variable_counter_target: "item" } %> <% if card.open? %> <% card_data[:card_not_now_url] = card_not_now_path(card) %> <% card_data[:card_closure_url] = card_closure_path(card) %> <% card_data[:action] = "mouseenter->navigable-list#hoverSelect" %> <% card_data[:card_assign_to_self_url] = card_self_assignment_path(card) %> <% end %> <%= card_article_tag card, class: "card", data: card_data, tabindex: 0 do %>
<%= link_to card_path(card), draggable: false, class: "card__link", title: card_title_tag(card), data: { action: "dialog#close", turbo_frame: "_top" } do %> <%= card.title %> <% end %>
<%= render "cards/display/preview/board", card: card %> <%= render "cards/display/preview/tags", card: card %> <%= render "cards/display/preview/steps", card: card %> <%= icon_tag "attachment", class: "card__attachments-indicator translucent" if card.has_attachments? %> <% if card.triaged? %> <%= card.column.name %> <% end %>

<%= card_html_title(card) %>

<%= render "cards/display/preview/columns", card: card %> <%= render "cards/display/common/stamp", card: card %>
<%= render "cards/display/preview/meta", card: card, preview: true %>
<%= render "cards/display/preview/boosts", card: card %> <%= render "cards/display/preview/comments", card: card %>
<%= render "cards/display/common/background", card: card %>
<% if card.entropic? %> <%= render "cards/display/preview/bubble", card: card %> <% end %> <% end %> ----

# Fizzy Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository. Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments. ## Deploy Default branch: `main` Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`. ## SaaS mode For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions. ## Architecture Overview ### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based) Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**: - Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes - URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...` - Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account` - The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path - Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions - Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context **Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler. ### Authentication & Authorization Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records. ### Entropy System Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity: - Account-level default entropy period - Board-level entropy override - Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating - Configurable via Account/Board settings ### UUID Primary Keys All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings): - Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests - Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records - `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests ### Background Jobs (Solid Queue) Database-backed job queue (no Redis): - Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob - Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account` - Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`. ### Sharded Full-Text Search Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`. ### Imports and exports Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances: - Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported) - Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB) - Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file` ## Coding style Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md. ---- <% card_data = { navigable_list_target: "item", css_variable_counter_target: "item" } %> <% if card.open? %> <% card_data[:card_not_now_url] = card_not_now_path(card) %> <% card_data[:card_closure_url] = card_closure_path(card) %> <% card_data[:action] = "mouseenter->navigable-list#hoverSelect" %> <% card_data[:card_assign_to_self_url] = card_self_assignment_path(card) %> <% end %> <%= card_article_tag card, class: "card", data: card_data, tabindex: 0 do %>
<%= link_to card_path(card), draggable: false, class: "card__link", title: card_title_tag(card), data: { action: "dialog#close", turbo_frame: "_top" } do %> <%= card.title %> <% end %>
<%= render "cards/display/preview/board", card: card %> <%= render "cards/display/preview/tags", card: card %> <%= render "cards/display/preview/steps", card: card %> <%= icon_tag "attachment", class: "card__attachments-indicator translucent" if card.has_attachments? %> <% if card.triaged? %> <%= card.column.name %> <% end %>

<%= card_html_title(card) %>

<%= render "cards/display/preview/columns", card: card %> <%= render "cards/display/common/stamp", card: card %>
<%= render "cards/display/preview/meta", card: card, preview: true %>
<%= render "cards/display/preview/boosts", card: card %> <%= render "cards/display/preview/comments", card: card %>
<%= render "cards/display/common/background", card: card %>
<% if card.entropic? %> <%= render "cards/display/preview/bubble", card: card %> <% end %> <% end %> ----

  config.before_record do |i|

    end
  end

  config.register_request_matcher :body_without_times do |r1, r2|
    b1 = (r1.body || "").gsub(/\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} UTC/, "<TIME>")

    b1 == b2
  end

  config.default_cassette_options = {
    match_requests_on: [ :method, :uri, :body_without_times ]
  }


You'll be able to access the app in development at http://app.fizzy.localhost:3006.

### Web Push Notifications

Fizzy uses VAPID (Voluntary Application Server Identification) keys to send browser push notifications. For notifications to work in development you'll need to generate a key pair and set these environment variables:

- `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`
- `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`

Generate them with the `web-push` gem:

```ruby
vapid_key = WebPush.generate_key

puts "VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY=#{vapid_key.private_key}"
puts "VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY=#{vapid_key.public_key}"
```

### Running tests

For fast feedback loops, unit tests can be run with:

```sh
bin/rails test
```

The full continuous integration tests can be run with:

```sh
bin/ci
```

### Database configuration

Fizzy works with SQLite by default and supports MySQL too. You can switch adapters with the `DATABASE_ADAPTER` environment variable. For example, to develop locally against MySQL:

```sh
DATABASE_ADAPTER=mysql bin/setup --reset
```

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

## Invocation order

We order methods vertically based on their invocation order. This helps us to understand the flow of the code.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    method_1
    method_2
  end

  private
    def method_1
      method_1_1
      method_1_2
    end
  
    def method_1_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_1_2
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2
      method_2_1
      method_2_2
    end
  
    def method_2_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

## To bang or not to bang

Should I call a method `do_something` or `do_something!`?

As a general rule, we only use `!` for methods that have a correspondent counterpart without `!`. In particular, we don’t use `!` to flag destructive actions. There are plenty of destructive methods in Ruby and Rails that do not end with `!`.

## Visibility modifiers

We don't add a newline under visibility modifiers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

require "application_system_test_case"

class DragAndDropTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  end

      Timeout.timeout(timeout) { sleep 0.05 until yield }
    end
end

require "application_system_test_case"

class DragAndDropTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    visit board_url(boards(:writebook))
  end

  test "dropping a card into another column moves it straight away, then saves" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    column = columns(:writebook_in_progress)

    drag card, onto: column

    assert_card_in column, card, wait: 0
    wait_for { card.reload.column == column }
  end

  test "the board doesn't wait for the save" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    column = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    delay_status_requests(3)

    drag card, onto: column

    assert_card_in column, card, wait: 0
    assert_nil card.reload.column
    wait_for { card.reload.column == column }
  end

  test "dropping a card back into its own column changes nothing" do
    card = cards(:layout)
    column = columns(:writebook_triage)
    expand column
    before = card_ids_in(column)
    record_status_requests

    drag card, onto: column

    assert_equal before, card_ids_in(column)
    assert_empty status_requests
  end

  test "a dropped card takes the place the server gives it, and keeps it once saved" do
    card = cards(:layout)
    column = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    expand columns(:writebook_triage)

    drag card, onto: column

    assert_equal expected_card_ids(column), card_ids_in(column)
    wait_for { card.reload.column == column }
    wait_for_board_refresh do
      perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob
    end
    assert_equal expected_card_ids(column), card_ids_in(column)
  end

  test "a card dropped on a column goes after the golden cards already there" do
    card = cards(:text)
    column = columns(:writebook_triage)
    expand columns(:writebook_in_progress)

    drag card, onto: column

    assert_equal expected_card_ids(column), card_ids_in(column)
    assert_equal [ cards(:logo), card, cards(:layout) ].map { |c| dom_id(c, :article) }, card_ids_in(column)
  end

  test "dropping a card on Not Now postpones it" do
    card = cards(:layout)
    expand columns(:writebook_triage)

    drag card, onto: "not-now"

    assert_selector "#not-now ##{dom_id(card, :article)}", visible: :all, wait: 0
    wait_for { card.reload.postponed? }
    assert_nil card.column
  end

  test "dropping a card on Done closes it" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)

    drag card, onto: "closed-cards"

    assert_selector "#closed-cards ##{dom_id(card, :article)}", visible: :all, wait: 0
    wait_for { card.reload.closed? }
  end

  test "dropping a card on Maybe? sends it back to triage" do
    card = cards(:shipping)
    expand "closed-cards"

    drag card, onto: "maybe"

    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}", wait: 0
    wait_for { card.reload.awaiting_triage? }
  end

  test "a save that fails reloads the board from the server" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    column = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    fail_status_requests

    drag card, onto: column

    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_nil card.reload.column
  end

  private
    def drag(card, onto:)
      target = onto.is_a?(String) ? find("##{onto}") : find("##{dom_id(onto)}")
      find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(target)
    end

    def expand(column_or_id)
      section = column_or_id.is_a?(String) ? column_or_id : dom_id(column_or_id)
      find("##{section} .cards__expander").click
      assert_selector "##{section}.is-expanded"
    end

    def assert_card_in(column, card, **options)
      assert_selector "##{dom_id(column)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}", visible: :all, **options
    end

    def card_ids_in(column)
      page.all("##{dom_id(column)} article.card", visible: :all).map { |article| article[:id] }
    end

    def expected_card_ids(column)
      column.cards.active.latest.with_golden_first.map { |card| dom_id(card, :article) }
    end

    def wait_for(timeout: 5)
      Timeout.timeout(timeout) { sleep 0.05 until yield }
    end

    # Holds back status saves so the test can see the board before the server answers
    def delay_status_requests(seconds)
      evaluate_script_wrapping_status_requests <<~JS
        new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, #{seconds * 1000})).then(() => original(input, init))
      JS
    end

    def fail_status_requests
      evaluate_script_wrapping_status_requests <<~JS
        Promise.resolve(new Response("", { status: 500 }))
      JS
    end

    def record_status_requests
      page.execute_script(<<~JS)
        window.__statusRequests = []
        const original = window.fetch
        window.fetch = (input, init) => {
          if (/\\/(triage|not_now|closure)/.test(String(input))) window.__statusRequests.push(String(input))
          return original(input, init)
        }
      JS
    end

    def status_requests
      page.evaluate_script("window.__statusRequests || []")
    end

    def evaluate_script_wrapping_status_requests(response_js)
      page.execute_script(<<~JS)
        const original = window.fetch
        window.fetch = (input, init) => {
          if (!/\\/(triage|not_now|closure)/.test(String(input))) return original(input, init)
          return #{response_js.strip.chomp}
        }
      JS
    end

    def wait_for_board_refresh
      page.execute_script("window.__boardMorphs = 0; document.addEventListener('turbo:morph', () => window.__boardMorphs++)")
      yield
      wait_for { page.evaluate_script("window.__boardMorphs") > 0 }
    end
end

That explains the timeout. Turbo's `fetchWithTurboHeaders` records each request ID, and the refresh broadcast carries that ID, so the dragging client skips the refresh for its own save. The board doesn't re-render after a drop, which is what "nothing shifting afterwards" needs. It also means the optimistic count and color updates are the only thing keeping the dragging client's view current, so they matter.

I also found a race in my test: it compared the DOM to the database before the save had finished. I'll rewrite that test so it waits for the save first, then checks the order the board showed on drop against the server's order and against a fresh page load.

require "application_system_test_case"

class DragAndDropTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    visit board_url(boards(:writebook))
  end

  test "dropping a card into another column moves it straight away, then saves" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    column = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    record_page_errors

    drag card, onto: column

    assert_card_in column, card, wait: 0
    assert_count "##{dom_id(column)}", "2", wait: 0
    assert_count "#maybe", "0", wait: 0
    wait_for { card.reload.column == column }
    assert_no_page_errors
  end

  test "the board doesn't wait for the save" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    column = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    delay_status_requests(3)

    drag card, onto: column

    assert_card_in column, card, wait: 0
    assert_nil card.reload.column
    wait_for { card.reload.column == column }
  end

  test "while a card is over a column, the column lights up and the card dims" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    column = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    pointer = page.driver.browser.action

    pointer.click_and_hold(find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").native).move_to(find("##{dom_id(column)}").native).perform

    assert_selector "##{dom_id(column)}.drag-and-drop__hover-container", visible: :all
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(card, :article)}.drag-and-drop__dragged-item", visible: :all

    pointer.release.perform

    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(column)}.drag-and-drop__hover-container", visible: :all
    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(card, :article)}.drag-and-drop__dragged-item", visible: :all
    wait_for { card.reload.column == column }
  end

  test "dropping a card back into its own column changes nothing" do
    card = cards(:layout)
    column = columns(:writebook_triage)
    expand column
    before = card_ids_in(column)
    record_status_requests

    drag card, onto: column

    assert_equal before, card_ids_in(column)
    assert_empty status_requests
  end

  test "a dropped card takes the place the server gives it, and keeps it once saved" do
    card = cards(:layout)
    column = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    expand columns(:writebook_triage)

    drag card, onto: column
    dropped_order = card_ids_in(column)

    wait_for { card.reload.column == column }
    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob

    assert_equal expected_card_ids(column), dropped_order

    visit board_url(boards(:writebook))
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(column)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}", visible: :all
    assert_equal dropped_order, card_ids_in(column)
  end

  test "a card dropped on a column goes after the golden cards already there" do
    card = cards(:text)
    column = columns(:writebook_triage)
    expand columns(:writebook_in_progress)

    drag card, onto: column

    assert_equal [ cards(:logo), card, cards(:layout) ].map { |c| dom_id(c, :article) }, card_ids_in(column)
    wait_for { card.reload.column == column }
    assert_equal expected_card_ids(column), card_ids_in(column)
  end

  test "dropping a card on Not Now postpones it" do
    card = cards(:layout)
    expand columns(:writebook_triage)

    drag card, onto: "not-now"

    assert_selector "#not-now ##{dom_id(card, :article)}.card--postponed", visible: :all, wait: 0
    wait_for { card.reload.postponed? }
    assert_nil card.column
  end

  test "dropping a card on Done closes it" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)

    drag card, onto: "closed-cards"

    assert_selector "#closed-cards ##{dom_id(card, :article)}", visible: :all, wait: 0
    wait_for { card.reload.closed? }
  end

  test "dropping a card on Maybe? sends it back to triage" do
    card = cards(:shipping)
    expand "closed-cards"

    drag card, onto: "maybe"

    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}", wait: 0
    wait_for { card.reload.awaiting_triage? }
  end

  test "a save that fails reloads the board from the server" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    column = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    fail_status_requests

    drag card, onto: column

    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_nil card.reload.column
  end

  private
    def drag(card, onto:)
      target = onto.is_a?(String) ? find("##{onto}") : find("##{dom_id(onto)}")
      find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(target)
    end

    def expand(column_or_id)
      section = column_or_id.is_a?(String) ? column_or_id : dom_id(column_or_id)
      find("##{section} .cards__expander").click
      assert_selector "##{section}.is-expanded"
    end

    def assert_card_in(column, card, **options)
      assert_selector "##{dom_id(column)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}", visible: :all, **options
    end

    def assert_count(section_selector, count, **options)
      assert_selector "#{section_selector} .cards__expander-count", exact_text: count, visible: :all, **options
    end

    def card_ids_in(column)
      page.all("##{dom_id(column)} article.card", visible: :all).map { |article| article[:id] }
    end

    def expected_card_ids(column)
      column.cards.active.latest.with_golden_first.map { |card| dom_id(card, :article) }
    end

    def wait_for(timeout: 5)
      Timeout.timeout(timeout) { sleep 0.05 until yield }
    end

    def record_page_errors
      page.execute_script(<<~JS)
        window.__pageErrors = []
        window.addEventListener("error", event => window.__pageErrors.push(event.message))
        window.addEventListener("unhandledrejection", event => window.__pageErrors.push(String(event.reason)))
      JS
    end

    def assert_no_page_errors
      assert_empty page.evaluate_script("window.__pageErrors || []")
    end

    # Holds back status saves so the test can see the board before the server answers
    def delay_status_requests(seconds)
      wrap_status_requests <<~JS
        new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, #{seconds * 1000})).then(() => original(input, init))
      JS
    end

    def fail_status_requests
      wrap_status_requests <<~JS
        Promise.resolve(new Response("", { status: 500 }))
      JS
    end

    def record_status_requests
      page.execute_script(<<~JS)
        window.__statusRequests = []
        const original = window.fetch
        window.fetch = (input, init) => {
          if (/\\/(triage|not_now|closure)/.test(String(input))) window.__statusRequests.push(String(input))
          return original(input, init)
        }
      JS
    end

    def status_requests
      page.evaluate_script("window.__statusRequests || []")
    end

    def wrap_status_requests(response_js)
      page.execute_script(<<~JS)
        const original = window.fetch
        window.fetch = (input, init) => {
          if (!/\\/(triage|not_now|closure)/.test(String(input))) return original(input, init)
          return #{response_js.strip.chomp}
        }
      JS
    end
end

Every mutation was caught by the intended tests, and the controller is restored. While reviewing the controller, I found three things to tighten:

1. Cards should only be draggable at the desktop breakpoint, matching the CSS, and the attribute needs updating when the viewport crosses that breakpoint.
2. `dragstart` currently calls `preventDefault()` on any drag inside the board, including ordinary links like the maximize buttons. It should only act on cards.
3. The constant name `ACTIVE_DESTINATIONS` is also used for golden-first ordering, which reads oddly. I'll rename it to say what it is.

I'll rewrite the controller with those fixes.

messages.content: This matters for real users. A valid drop produces no click. A cancelled drag, including one released over empty space, ends with a `mouseup` and `click` on the card's link under the drag start point, so releasing a card over a non-target would open the card. That needs handling in the controller. I'll swallow that one click when a drag ends with no drop (`dropEffect === "none"`), and remove the swallowing listener on a short timer so it can't eat a later, real click. First I'll check how soon the click arrives after `dragend`, so I pick a safe timer.

messages.content: The timing is tight: `dragend` fires at about 772ms, the `setTimeout(0)` at 782ms, and `mouseup` and `click` at about 798ms. A timer is therefore too fragile. The reliable boundary is the next mouse press: a click can only follow a mousedown, so I'll ignore the click after a cancelled drag until the next `mousedown`, and the listeners remove themselves either way.

messages.content:
Drag-and-drop is implemented. The board now supports dragging cards between columns, Maybe?, Not Now, and Done, with the board updating on drop and the save following in the background.

The drag-and-drop Stimulus controller was missing from the repo (only the stylesheet existed), so I wrote it. Everything else is wiring into the existing views and endpoints.

## What changed

- **`app/javascript/controllers/drag_and_drop_controller.js`** (new): the drag handling.
  - On drop, the card moves in the DOM immediately, and the counts and card color update with it. The save runs in the background and does not wait on the server.
  - A drop into the same list does nothing and sends no request, so cards never reorder within a column.
  - The card lands where the server will sort it. Cards go to the top of a list, except in golden-first lists (the columns and Maybe?), where a non-golden card goes after the golden ones.
  - Saves use the existing JSON endpoints, which return 204. Saves for one card run in order.
  - If a save fails, the board reloads from the server, since the server is the source of truth.
  - Dragging only works at desktop widths (≥640px), matching the CSS.
- **Board views** (`_columns`, `_column`, `_stream`, `_not_now`, `_closed`): the board is wired to the controller, and each drop target declares its destination.
- **`cards/display/_preview.html.erb`**: every card carries its triage, not-now, and closure URLs, so closed cards can also be dragged out of Done.

## Things I found while testing

- Turbo skips the board refresh that follows a save when the client made the request itself. So the dragging client doesn't re-render after a drop, which is why the optimistic counts and colors matter.
- Releasing a drag that nothing accepts fires a click on the card's link, which would open the card. The controller ignores that click until the next mouse press.

## Verification

- New `test/system/drag_and_drop_test.rb`: 15 browser tests covering the instant move, the un-awaited save, same-column no-op, placement matching the server's order (with and without golden cards), each status destination, the failure reload, the hover and dragged styles, and mobile behavior. They passed on repeated runs.
- I broke the controller in targeted ways (wait-then-move, always-append placement, allowing same-column drops, removing the click guard), and the matching tests failed each time.
- Full suites: 1538 unit and integration tests and 30 system tests, all passing. RuboCop is clean.

## Caveats

- Placement mirrors the server's sort order in `drag_and_drop_controller.js`. If that ordering changes on the server, the client rule has to change too.
- Dropping onto a collapsed column adds the card there, where it stays hidden until the column is expanded. The count updates, but nothing expands.
- Only headless Chrome was tested. I didn't check Firefox or Safari.
